title: Checkpointed validation & soft-degrade behavior for streamed tool/function outputs
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Define acceptance criteria and rollout plan for a checkpointed validation layer that runs during streaming responses which call external tools/functions. Objective: ensure schema correctness checkpoints, allow graceful continuation with soft-degrade markers, and provide clear telemetry and repair primitives for downstream consumers.
background: Customers use streaming LLM outputs with embedded tool/function calls. Current failures are opaque: partial JSON blobs, mid-stream schema mismatches, and silent tool-call retries that break client parsers. We need a pragmatic contract so SDKs and customers can rely on stable checkpoints with clear error semantics and recovery paths.
requirements: Introduce a lightweight checkpoint frame emitted every N objects/bytes with a checkpoint_id and validation_status.
Define an error taxonomy for streaming tool outputs: transient, repairable, unrecoverable, schema-mismatch.
Allow the runtime to emit soft-degrade frames when a downstream tool is unavailable, including suggested fallback model/variant or placeholder object.
Expose idempotency tokens and replay hints for repairable tool-call failures so clients or gateways can request a replay or accept a repaired result.
Provide telemetry hooks: checkpoint_pass/fail metrics, first-fail-classifier tag, and per-request validation latency.
SDK contract: parsers should be able to resume/skip to the next checkpoint with clear markers and resolve partial objects with a reconciliation API.
Backpressure and rate signals must be preserved — checkpoint emission must not violate latency SLOs for low-latency flows (configurable pacing).
non_goals: This work will not introduce new cryptographic signing or tamper-proof checkpoints (out of scope for initial rollout).
We are not changing the underlying tool invocation semantics (retry policies) beyond emitting metadata and replay hints.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint frames: For streaming responses with structured payloads, the runtime emits a recognized JSON-ish frame '<CHECKPOINT>' every checkpoint_interval with fields: checkpoint_id, offset_token, validation_status, and optional suggested_fallback (strings only).

Validation statuses: At least three statuses must be supported: PASS, SOFT_FAIL, HARD_FAIL. PASS means schema validated, SOFT_FAIL means schema deviation but repairable/filled with placeholders, HARD_FAIL means terminal and stream must include an explicit termination frame.

Soft-degrade behavior: When a tool invocation fails transiently, the stream may emit a SOFT_FAIL checkpoint and include a placeholder object with a repair_hint and replay_token. The stream must continue and mark the placeholder with a __degraded=true flag. Consumers can choose to accept or request replay.

Replay primitive: The runtime must return a replay_token at checkpoint emission for any repairable failure and a documented endpoint in the Console/SDK to request a replay of the segment identified by checkpoint_id and offset_token. Replay attempts must be idempotent and include causal metadata.

Client SDK parsing: SDKs (Python and TypeScript) must provide a resume_to_checkpoint(checkpoint_id) API that safely skips partial objects and returns the next validated object boundary. Unit tests will cover resumptions across partial multi-object streams.

Schema mismatch telemetry: When a checkpoint emits SOFT_FAIL or HARD_FAIL, an event with tags {checkpoint_id, request_id, first_fail_classifier, model, tool} is recorded and visible in Console traces within 60s.

Backpressure: Checkpoint emission must not increase P50 token latency by more than 10ms in default pacing mode. Performance tests simulate 5K qps with mixed small/large sequence lengths and assert latency budgets.

E2E tests: Create 5 end-to-end regression suites including: normal PASS flows, injected transient tool failures leading to SOFT_FAIL, injected schema-mismatch leading to HARD_FAIL with explicit termination, SDK resume flows, and replay-request flows. All tests must pass on staging runtime-1.25.
risks: Added checkpoint frames increase bandwidth and may require SDK parsing changes — risk of breaking naive consumers.
Replay semantics could be abused to re-run costly tool calls — needs quota/guardrails in Dedicated/Private plans.
Incorrect classifier/first_fail tagging could noise alerts — requires calibration and a small pilot.
open_questions: What default checkpoint_interval should we pick for hosted customers vs Dedicated? (tradeoff: latency vs. recoverability).
Do we permit automatic server-side repair (best-effort filling) or always return placeholders for client-driven repair?
What authentication/authorization model is required for replay endpoints in Private deployments?
implementation_notes: Server: Add light-weight checkpoint emitter in streaming runtime that can be toggled per-route. Configurable interval and optional size-based emission.
Tooling: Add replay_token generation at tool-gateway layer; token encodes causal chain + segment window and is HMAC'd with service key.
SDKs: Implement resume_to_checkpoint and accept_degraded(accept:boolean) helper to surface placeholder objects clearly to application code.
Console: Dashboard tile showing checkpoint pass/fail rate per model and heatmap of first_fail_classifiers; add link to replay request from trace detail pane.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable checkpointing for 5% of tenant traffic for non-sensitive routes. Collect telemetry and test SDK parsing with opt-in flag.
Phase 2 (beta): Expand to customers who opt-in; provide Replay API in Console and SDK; open limited docs and sample apps.
Phase 3 (general): Turn on default checkpoint emission for hosted API; add admin toggle per-workspace in Dedicated/Private.
